Ternium Argentina SA Names New Chief Operating Officer Amid Steady Market Demand

BUENOS AIRES, June 21—Ternium Argentina SA, one of the country’s largest steel producers, announced Friday the appointment of Laura Benítez as its new Chief Operating Officer, effective July 1. The move comes as the Buenos Aires-based company continues to focus on operational efficiency and sustained demand in the domestic steel market.

Benítez, who previously held senior management roles at the firm, will succeed Ricardo Martínez, who is retiring after more than three decades with Ternium Argentina SA. The company said in a statement that Benítez’s experience in production and supply chain management positions her well to lead ongoing modernization projects at the plant in San Nicolás.

“Ternium Argentina is committed to driving operational excellence. Laura brings a deep understanding of our processes and a record of delivering results,” CEO Jorge Brunetti said. “We thank Ricardo for his outstanding leadership and dedication.”

Industry analysts noted the appointment comes as steel consumption in Argentina remains stable, supported by construction and automotive sector orders. “Ternium’s decision ensures continuity in management at a time when the local steel industry is navigating both challenges and opportunities,” said Martín Iglesias, a Buenos Aires-based metals sector analyst.

The Argentine Chamber of Steel welcomed the announcement, citing Benítez’s technical background and engagement with industry initiatives. The company reported crude steel output of 2.5 million tons last year, maintaining its position as a key supplier in the region.

Ternium Argentina SA employs more than 4,000 people in Argentina. The company said no other management changes are planned at this time.
